content.thinking:
I'm planning the whole scene in one careful pass without testing along the way: a Genshin-style roadside shrine with a vermilion torii gate roughly 3 meters tall, gold caps, a black kasagi beam and nameplate, set on a stone plinth around 3 meters across. I'm adding two glowing stone lanterns, a small hokora shrine with its own roof, and an offerings table with a sake barrel, fruit, and rice.

Now I'm fleshing out the rest of the offerings and decorations -- incense, shide paper streamers, shimenawa rope with tassels, fox statues, a bell, ema plaques, glowing paper lanterns, and maybe a stylized tree -- aiming to keep it rich but still manageable. I'm setting up a single root joint called "base" that all parts attach to, since joints are only needed for moving pieces, and I'm building helper functions for boxes and cylinders, with the hokora roof made from a low-segment cone rotated into a pyramid shape. For materials I'm mixing toon-shaded cel paints for the big surfaces with flat colors for the glowing elements, keeping an eye on the color budget.

Now I'm working out the stone plinth material using a mottled cel paint, then laying out the scene geometry -- a stone disk base, a flagstone path made of staggered boxes leading toward the viewer, and small cone-shaped grass tufts scattered around, keeping each as a separate part since the total count stays well under the limit. I'm positioning the torii gate with tapered cylindrical pillars on either side.

Writing torii beam details...

Tassels gold at the rope ends with spheres and cones, then thinking through hanging chochin lanterns from the nuki — flat emissive orange ellipsoids with gold cap rings, dark rib torus details, and a tassel hanging below each.

Now I'm designing stone toro lanterns to flank the torii pillars: hexagonal base cylinders, slender poles, nakadai platforms, and a firebox built from corner posts framing a glowing inner box, topped with a lathe-profiled roof and gem-shaped finial.

Writing moss/stone paint logic...

Now I'm planning the hokora shrine at the back: stone step platform, a dark red wood body box with gold trim, and lattice-textured doors using an SVG plane.

For the roof I'm using a pyramid cone with overhang, ridge, crossed gold chigi finials, and a wide 1.6-unit span, plus a veranda deck with railings and four posts. I'm adding offerings in front -- a banded sake barrel, stacked fruit on a tray, mochi spheres, an incense burner with glowing sticks, tea cup, a sakaki branch vase, and a slatted saisen-bako money box, along with a hanging rope and gold suzu bell.

Now I'm sketching stone kitsune statues flanking the steps, built from a haunch, chest, head, snout, ears, tail, and red bib, sized and mirrored on pedestals near the lanterns, facing the viewer. I'm also placing a sakura tree in the back left with a swept trunk and clustered pink low-poly canopy.

For atmosphere, I'm scattering a few flat pink petal cards on the ground near the shrine rather than floating ones, and adding glowing wisp spheres plus an upward-facing glowing sigil decal -- rings, an eight-pointed star, gold and cyan glow -- on the plinth in front of the shrine.

Now I'm sizing the ground base: a lathed disc around 2.5m radius with a slightly raised grass-like rim, settling everything onto a shared ground height of 0.14 so pillars and props sink in consistently.

I'm also laying out a stone path running along z from 2.4 to -0.4, made of slightly offset flagstone boxes, with gravel bordering it and grass mottling elsewhere, all handled through a paint function that checks position to decide color.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for the build, with a root joint and a shorthand for placing parts with consistent bone and position, using flat geometry where appropriate but disabling it for textured planes.

Settling on `string | Paint` for fill values, with helper functions for boxes and cylinders. I'm defining the color palette: vermilion red, dark lacquer black, gold paint, wood grain texture, and white paper tones for the piece.

Adding remaining colors...

Designing the SVG textures: a nameplate with a geometric flower emblem instead of kanji, a red door lattice with gold lines, a zigzag white shide paper strip, a simple pink petal ellipse, and a green grass blade polygon for ground detail.

Scattering the grass and card elements randomly across the ground radius, avoiding the path, over 60 frames. Adding ema plaques with a fox face design hanging on a small wooden rack near the right side with two posts and a bar, plus building the torii gate pillar geometry.

Writing torii gate code...

Adding the stone base slab under the pillar, then working on the shimenawa sacred rope with its sagging catmull-rom curve and straw-colored twist, plus shide paper streamers hanging at knot points along the rope.

Each shide card leans along the flow direction so it faces outward, with gold sphere-and-cone tassels finishing the rope ends. Now I'm positioning hanging chochin lanterns off the nuki crossbeam near the rope span, working out the cord attachment points to avoid clipping the shimenawa.

Let me try hanging the rope higher between the nuki and kasagi instead, near y 2.6, though that risks crossing the plaque on the center post—placing it slightly in front should work even if it partially obscures the plaque. I'll settle on lanterns hanging from the nuki at x=±0.7 with their lower ends at z=1.2.

Actually the rope still conflicts with the lantern bodies at that position, so I'm moving the lanterns outside the pillars entirely, near x=±1.35 along the nuki overhang, with cords dropping from y 2.3 to a lantern center around y 1.95, keeping the rope confined between the pillars where it won't intersect anything. For the chochin lanterns themselves I'm scaling a sphere to give an oval shape, adding a soft glow, and adding dark torus rings as ribs around the surface.

Writing stone base geometry...

Still laying out the hokora shrine...

Working out the eave overhang geometry, then placing the suzu bell and its hanging rope with twisted red/white cords and tassel near the front, while checking the saisen offering box position doesn't collide with the bell placement.

I'm shifting the saisen-bako to z=0.0 centered on the path between the fox statues, adjusting the bell rope's endpoint height to clear its top, and planning a small offering table to the left near the foxes.

Now I'm placing the offerings table off the path and checking the ema rack position on the right against lantern and torii pillar spacing, nudging it to avoid overlaps with the chochin lanterns and nuki beams.

I'm positioning the back-left tree and offerings table, checking all elements still fit within the ground radius, and enlarging the ground to 2.8 for margin. I'm defining the fox figures as a function placing them symmetrically with pedestal bases.

Still building fox anatomy...

Adding ears, eyes, red bib collar, bell, and tail details, then working out cone orientation for the forward-facing snout using rotation and direction vectors. I'm settling on a cel-shaded stone texture with moss for the fox, then shifting to design the tree trunk instead of the sakaki branch.

For the tree, I'm sweeping a curved trunk with bark texture and branches, adding an icosahedron-based canopy of pink spheres with mottled cel shading, and checking total height stays under the torii gate limit while keeping the trunk within ground bounds. I'm also planning scattered floating petal cards above the ground with randomized positions and flow directions for a drifting effect.

Now I'm adding glowing cyan wisp spheres near the shrine and a sigil, plus an offerings table with a box top, four leg boxes, a red cloth runner, and a wooden sake barrel with gold bands and a dark lid placed on top.

I'm continuing to lay out the table items: a lacquered red fruit tray with a pyramid of orange spheres, a stack of flattened white mochi on a small wooden stand, positioned along the table's x-axis, with a small incense bowl planned at the front.

Instead of placing incense on the table, I decide to put it on the ground slightly off to the side, with a stone bowl, sand, and four slanted incense sticks with glowing tips. I also add two tiny sake cups with gold rims on the table, then move on to planning the ema rack with two support posts.

The crossbar and small tilted roof plank sit atop the posts, with five small ema plaques hung below, spaced and facing forward with simple texture fronts. I check that a stone water basin near the torii pillar doesn't overlap too closely with existing elements, keeping distances in mind.

Working through the basin position with a cylindrical stone shape, water disc, and bamboo ladle laid across the rim, I adjust the lanterns to symmetric positions so their radii don't collide with the pillar or basin, verifying distances between each object stay clear.

I settle on a part count of roughly 250, then design the ground texture with layered cel paints for dirt, gravel, and grass, blending a gravel path through the center and scattering mottled grass patterns elsewhere, before shaping the ground's lathe profile as a wide flat disc with a slightly raised rim.

I'm adding a decorative stone border around the perimeter using scattered icosahedron rocks, laying flagstone boxes along the path at regular intervals slightly raised above the gravel, and defining a shared stone paint function for consistent coloring, then starting on grass tuft cards using a textured grass billboard approach.

Now I'm designing a sigil in SVG with concentric circles in cyan and gold, an eight-point star, and a ring of small dots on a transparent background.

Positioning the sigil plane above the stones so it doesn't get obscured, checking clearance against the torii pillars and crossbeam, then setting up the plane geometry facing upward with the sigil texture and glow applied.

Now I'm adding small hanging paper lanterns at the hokora eaves, placing a pair of chochin on either side with cords connecting them up to the roofline, each lantern given a warm orange glow with a slightly elongated shape.

Setting up helper functions now—a generic part creator that takes geometry, color, and position, then box/cylinder/sphere shortcuts built on top of it for quickly placing shapes with consistent bone attachment and flat shading.

Still writing stone tower geometry...

Working out the hokora roof lathe shape with square cross-section from 4-segment spin, checking the eave width against body dimensions, then eyeing where the roof front edge and body front face line up so the bell doesn't clip through the overhang.

Still working out deck and body placement...

Now I'm sketching door panels on the front face with gold frame accents, and placing corner pillars at the body's edges to anchor the structure visually.

I'm deciding on dark lacquer pillars with gold bands instead of solid gold, then moving to the fox ears and scattering details using random placement. For the rope elements, I'm sweeping a tube along a Catmull-Rom curve through sampled points to create the twisted straw rope, and generating evenly spaced frames along that path to position the hanging shide paper strips.

Now I'm checking which branches use the bone-driven sweep for the tree, and planning the canopy as faceted icosahedron spheres. I'm double-checking which imports actually get used in the final file—confirming noise, paint, mottle, catmull, frame, rng, glow, and THREE are all needed while dropping unused ones like aim—and sketching the SVG polygon for the emblem shape.

Now I'm designing the fox-face plaque SVG with its ears, eyes, and stroke proportions, deciding the plane geometry should serve as the plaque itself with a thin backing box behind it for depth, then moving on to the door SVG with its base rectangle fill.

Writing shide zigzag paper SVG...

Now sketching the nameplate SVG with a gold outer border, dark inner panel, and a six-petal flower emblem.

For the petal and grass sprites I'm defining small viewBox shapes with pink ellipses and green blade polygons, sized consistently at 64px. Also noting I need to keep texture planes non-flat where needed and confirm default facing direction for front/back planes before writing the final file.
